Definition: genitive case from G4571 and G846, also dative case of the same, σεαυτῷ, and accusative case σεαυτόν, likewise contracted σαυτοῦ, σαυτῷ, and σαυτόν, respectively; of (with, to) thyself:--thee, thine own self, (thou) thy(-self).
BiblicalUsage: Seautou is thyself, and Paul turns it on Timothy twice: exercise thyself rather unto godliness, and take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine, for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that a teacher's first flock is himself — take heed to thyself first, and the doctrine will follow.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
